result.title: Teach with Blinks: Breaking Linguistic Momentum in On-Policy Distillation for Fine-Grained Multimodal Perception
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) has emerged as an effective post-training approach to improving fine-grained perception in multimodal large language models by amortizing costly inference-time zooming operations into a single-pass recipe. However, vanilla OPD is inherently susceptible to linguistic momentum: the teacher can follow the student's erroneous prefixes, thus weakening corrective supervision. To address this, we propose Blink On-Policy Distillation (BlinkOPD), in which the teacher "blinks" at every token: it reads the same prefix once with its eyes open and once with its eyes closed. A first-glance gain further strengthens the correction on rollouts that conflict with the teacher. By extracting more effective supervision from each on-policy trajectory, BlinkOPD achieves state-of-the-art average performance across six fine-grained benchmarks using only 500 training images (12x less data) than existing OPD methods. Beyond fine-grained perception, BlinkOPD also demonstrates strong zero-shot improvements across ten held-out benchmarks spanning general visual perception, visual hallucination, and multimodal reasoning abilities. Code: https://github.com/Supltz/BlinkOPD

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BlinkOPD：在 on-policy 蒸馏中让教师对同一前缀分别在有视觉输入与无视觉输入下各读一次，用两次预测差（first-glance gain）强化纠正，以缓解教师被学生错误前缀带偏的「语言惯性」，把推理期放大操作摊销进单次前向，仅用 500 张训练图便在六个细粒度基准上取得最优平均表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「眨眼」式视觉消融实质是在衡量教师监督是否真正依赖图像，与 LVR 关注的视觉旁路、信息坍缩及训练信号归因直接相关，该 gain 是否可作视觉证据使用程度的度量可供核查。
